items.title: Lorigerlimab Plus Docetaxel Phase 2 Trial for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This completed phase 2 trial tested whether adding lorigerlimab (an immunotherapy drug) to standard docetaxel chemotherapy could delay cancer progression in 150 men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Participants received up to 35 cycles of lorigerlimab with up to 10 cycles of docetaxel and prednisone. Results from this completed trial could show if the combination works better than chemotherapy alone.

items.title: ONC-392 Combined with Lutetium PSMA Treatment Phase 1/2 Trial
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial is testing ONC-392 (an immunotherapy) combined with Pluvicto (lutetium-177 PSMA therapy) in metastatic CRPC patients who have progressed after hormonal therapy and up to 2 chemotherapy treatments but have not yet received Pluvicto. The study is no longer enrolling new patients but is still following participants to assess safety and effectiveness.

items.title: PSMA-PET Imaging Study Comparing Two Scanning Methods
items.summary: This phase 2 imaging study compares two types of PET scans (18F-DCFPyL PSMA-PET versus 18F-NaF-PET) to determine which is better at detecting sites of metastatic prostate cancer in the body. Participants receive injections of radioactive tracers and undergo whole-body scans. The study is no longer enrolling but continues to follow participants.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone for Chemotherapy-Naïve mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have not yet received chemotherapy. The study compares xaluritamig (a novel immunotherapy) combined with abiraterone against standard treatments (docetaxel, cabazitaxel, or abiraterone alone). The primary goal is to determine if the combination improves overall survival.

items.title: DS9051b Phase 1 Trial for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This first-in-human phase 1 trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to test the safety, tolerability, and early signs of effectiveness of DS9051b, a new investigational drug. The study is also testing this drug in patients with adrenocortical carcinoma.

items.title: AZD8359 STEAP2 Immunotherapy First-in-Human Trial for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial is recruiting men with metastatic prostate cancer to test AZD8359, an experimental immunotherapy that targets STEAP2 protein on cancer cells. The study has multiple parts testing different doses, dosing schedules, and delivery methods to find the safest and most effective approach.

items.title: Genetic Biomarker Study for Predicting Metastatic Recurrence
items.summary: This completed study used next-generation sequencing to analyze genetic changes in localized or locally advanced prostate cancer tissue. The goal was to identify genetic biomarkers that could predict which patients are at higher risk for metastatic recurrence. Such biomarkers could help identify patients who need more aggressive treatment.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial of Ifinatamab Deruxtecan for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial is recruiting men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to compare ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd, an antibody-drug conjugate) against standard chemotherapy. The study aims to determine if I-DXd helps patients live longer overall and delays cancer progression better than chemotherapy.

items.title: AAA817 Phase 2/3 Trial After Lutetium PSMA Treatment Failure
items.summary: This phase 2/3 trial is recruiting patients with PSMA-positive metastatic CRPC who have already received hormonal therapy, chemotherapy, and Pluvicto (lutetium-177 PSMA therapy) but whose cancer has continued to progress. The study compares AAA817 (an investigational drug) against standard treatment options for this heavily pre-treated population.

items.title: FG-3246 Phase 2 Trial for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 2 trial is recruiting men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have received one prior hormonal therapy but no chemotherapy yet. The study tests FG-3246, an antibody-drug conjugate targeting CD46 protein, evaluating its safety, effectiveness, and how the body processes the drug.

items.title: Phase 3: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial is recruiting men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) who have not yet received hormonal therapy or chemotherapy for metastatic disease. The study compares mevrometostat combined with enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone to see if the combination delays cancer progression.

items.title: Phase 3: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial is recruiting men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have not previously received enzalutamide or abiraterone. The study tests whether adding mevrometostat (PF-06821497) to enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone in controlling cancer progression.

items.title: Olaparib Plus Radium-223 Phase 1/2 Trial for Bone Metastases
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests combining olaparib (a PARP inhibitor pill) with radium-223 (radioactive injections) for men with castration-resistant prostate cancer that has spread to bones and other sites. The study is no longer enrolling and aims to find the best dose and evaluate whether this combination safely slows cancer growth.

items.title: Phase 1 Safety Study of Xaluritamig for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1 trial is recruiting men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to determine the safety profile and appropriate dosing of xaluritamig, a novel immunotherapy drug. This early-stage study focuses on establishing whether the drug can be given safely before moving to larger effectiveness trials.

items.title: DCC-2812 Phase 1 Trial for Advanced Prostate and Other Cancers
items.summary: This phase 1 trial is recruiting patients with advanced or metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, renal cell carcinoma, and urothelial carcinoma. The study evaluates the safety and early activity of DCC-2812, which activates GCN2 enzyme to potentially slow cancer growth.

items.title: Study Validating 15 Drug-Targetable Proteins as Biomarkers in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This observational study is evaluating 15 membrane proteins (including PSMA, B7-H3, STEAP1, and others) that could be targeted by antibody-drug conjugates. Researchers are testing tumor samples from different prostate cancer subtypes to determine which proteins are most commonly expressed and whether they predict patient outcomes. Results could guide future targeted therapy selection.

items.title: Novel Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes Treatment Resistance in mCRPC
items.summary: This research study developed new drugs that simultaneously block both BRD4 and AKT proteins, which are involved in treatment resistance in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Lab studies showed that compound 21d effectively overcame resistance driven by c-MYC, a protein that often causes single-agent AKT inhibitors to fail. This represents a potential new treatment approach for resistant disease.

items.title: International Analysis of Prostate Cancer Drug Approvals and Clinical Benefit
items.summary: This study analyzed reimbursement decisions for 20 prostate cancer drug-indication pairs across eight countries (Canada, France, England, Wales, Scotland, Spain, Italy, Portugal) from 2005-2024. The analysis examined which drugs were approved, their clinical benefit ratings, and whether they improved overall survival or quality of life. Canada and France had the highest approval rates for prostate cancer drugs.

items.title: Stereotactic Radiation for Supraclavicular Lymph Node Metastases in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This study examined outcomes in 16 men with metastatic prostate cancer who developed spread to lymph nodes above the collarbone (supraclavicular area). All received stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT), typically 35 Gy in 5 treatments. No serious side effects occurred, and the treatment appeared safe and effective for this uncommon metastatic site.

items.title: Machine Learning Model Predicts Survival in Prostate Cancer with Bone Metastases
items.source: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
items.summary: Researchers developed a machine learning model using data from 3,378 men with prostate cancer that spread to bones who did not have surgery. The model predicts overall survival, with Gleason score (cancer aggressiveness) being the most important factor—more important than tumor size. The model could help doctors identify high-risk patients who need more aggressive treatment.

items.title: Novel ALDH7A1 Inhibitors for Prostate Cancer Treatment
items.source: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
items.summary: This research identified new drugs that irreversibly block ALDH7A1, an enzyme that drives prostate cancer growth. The compounds were selective for ALDH7A1 over similar enzymes. ALDH7A1 is an emerging target in prostate cancer, particularly metastatic castration-resistant disease, but selective inhibitors have been lacking until now.

items.title: Meta-Analysis: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This meta-analysis combined data from 1,580 patients across 21 clinical trials testing immune checkpoint inhibitors for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer without biomarker selection. At 1 year, 63% were alive and 41% had stable disease at 6 months. Combining immunotherapy with other treatments showed better results than immunotherapy alone, though overall benefits were modest in unselected patients.

items.title: Zoledronic Acid Protects Bone Health During Enzalutamide Plus ADT Treatment
items.summary: This phase 2 trial (BonEnza study) randomized 89 men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer to receive ADT plus enzalutamide with or without zoledronic acid (a bone-protecting drug). After 18 months, patients who received zoledronic acid had significantly better bone mineral density and bone quality scores, suggesting the drug helps prevent bone weakening from hormonal treatments.
